P1.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
P1.bio: Mr. Utterson is a Gaunt Street lawyer, kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and friend of Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past, troubled by old sins. After Enfield showed him a sinister door and named its user, Utterson studied Jekyll's will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde. He consulted Lanyon, watched the by-street door, and accosted Hyde. Later he stayed after Jekyll's dinner and promised to help Hyde for Jekyll's sake. He then identified Sir Danvers Carew's body and searched Hyde's rooms. He is now obsessed with finding and seeing Hyde.

P7.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
P7.bio: Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, connoisseur, and friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon. He is large, well-made, smooth-faced, with a slyish cast, showing capacity and kindness and warm affection for Utterson. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. After dinner with Utterson, Jekyll refused to hear more of Hyde, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He is now painfully situated, his position strange and not mended by talking.

P3.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
P3.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, living in Soho and served by Poole and an old woman landlady. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred, impressing beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque. Utterson later accosted him at the by-street door, and Hyde gave his Soho address before disappearing inside. Jekyll called him poor Hyde and asked Utterson to help him. The maid then saw Hyde beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He is now a fugitive with few acquaintances and no traceable family.

P13.bio: Inspector Newcomen is a Scotland Yard officer investigating the murder of Sir Danvers Carew, working with Mr. Utterson, who guides the investigation. He is a professional police officer. He narrated the maid's account and showed the broken stick. Utterson took him to Hyde's house, where the old woman let them search and they found the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book. He found several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank. He now plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.

P12.bio: Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. The maid servant saw Hyde beat him to death with a cane. His body was found mangled in the lane. A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson was found on him. Utterson identified the body as Sir Danvers Carew. He is now dead, murdered by Hyde.

P11.tagline: Witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
P11.bio: The maid servant is a servant who witnesses the murder of Sir Danvers Carew by Edward Hyde. She is a maid servant. She saw Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane. She fainted at the horror of the murder. She woke at two and called the police. She is now the witness who sees Hyde murder Carew.
